chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to him, 'May Allah improve you! We have a neighbor who is a butcher; a Jew comes to him and slaughters [an animal] for him, so that the Jews buy from him.' He said, 'Do not eat from his slaughter, and do not buy from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a butcher who slaughters for a Jew to buy?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a specific ruling on meat from a butcher who slaughters for a Jew to purchase, advising against both eating and buying it. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the context of the transaction and the identity of the buyer, distinguishing it from general rulings on the People of the Book. The ruling underscores the importance of ensuring the purity and validity of consumption in daily life according to Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Al Ahmasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! There is a neighbour of ours, a butcher, so a Jew comes over to him and slaughters for him so that the Jews buy from him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat from his slaughter, and do not buy from him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from al-Husayn al-Ahmasiy who has said the following:

“Once a man said to ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, we have a neighbor who is a butcher and he brings Jews who slaughter for him so that Jews can buy from him.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not use for food what he sells and do not buy from him.’”
